devdoc.details: Exchange rate between stToken and wstToken floats, you can convert your wstToken for more stToken over time. Exchange rate increases as the frax msig mints new stToken corresponding to the staking yield and drops it into the vault (wstToken contract). There is a short time period, “cycles” which the exchange rate increases linearly over. This is to prevent gaming the exchange rate (MEV). The cycles are constant length, but calling syncRewards slightly into a would-be cycle keeps the same would-be endpoint (so cycle ends are every X seconds). Someone must call syncRewards, which queues any new stToken in the contract to be added to the redeemable amount. wstToken adheres to ERC-4626 vault specs  Mint vs Deposit mint() - deposit targeting a specific number of wstToken out deposit() - deposit knowing a specific number of stToken in

# Liquid Staking

{% hint style="info" %}
Liquid Staking: <https://accumulated.finance/stake>
{% endhint %}

### Overview

Liquid Staking in Accumulated Finance allows users to stake assets on supported Proof-of-Stake (PoS) chains and receive Liquid Staking Tokens (LSTs) at a 1:1 ratio. These LSTs represent the staked assets, accrue staking rewards, and remain usable within broader DeFi ecosystem (DEXs, lending, borrowing, leverage staking, etc.). The protocol offers flexible withdrawal options, including an NFT-based system or instant withdrawals from pending deposits pools when liquidity is available.

### Key Features

* **1:1 LST Issuance**: Receive LSTs equivalent to staked assets, maintaining full value representation.
* **Reward Accrual**: LSTs automatically earn staking rewards from the underlying PoS chain.
* **DeFi Compatibility**: Use LSTs in Accumulated Finance’s lending markets or other protocols.
* **Flexible Withdrawals**: Redeem staked assets via NFT-based withdrawals or instantly from liquidity pools.

### Benefits

* **Liquidity**: LSTs unlock staked capital for use in DeFi, avoiding traditional staking lockups.
* **Passive Income**: Earn staking rewards without managing validators.
* **Flexibility**: Choose between NFT-based or instant withdrawals based on your needs.
* **Cross-Chain Utility**: Seamlessly use LSTs across supported EVM networks via AEVM.

Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory.

Ethereum nonproxy wstACME staking-share ledger only. Current primary product API marks the Ethereum pool sunset=false and hidden=false; the Arbitrum wACME and BSC VLX pools are explicitly sunset and excluded. Wrapper full flattened source and ABI have Sourcify match creation/runtime grades, not exact_match. No bridge method is admitted.

Underlying stACME and wstACME share quantities use 8 decimals, inherited from underlying token decimals. deposit and mint pull only caller stACME and issue receiver shares. withdraw and redeem burn owner shares, requiring existing share allowance when caller differs from owner; no approval, permit or other authority is granted. Recipients need not be caller. Zero native value is required.

deposit rounds shares down and rejects zero shares; mint rounds required assets up; withdraw rounds required shares up; redeem rounds assets down and rejects zero assets. Empty supply uses one-to-one raw-unit conversion. No slippage/minimum-output parameter or wrapper fee exists in these bodies.

The xERC4626 ledger increases stored assets after deposits and decreases them before exits. totalAssets includes linearly unlocked prior-cycle rewards, not the entire observed token balance. syncRewards is permissionless fixed accounting only: it requires the prior cycle ended and positive surplus, incorporates the previous reward amount, and schedules surplus over a rounded next cycle (extended near the end). It does not pull funds or choose a recipient. Deposits do not themselves invoke syncRewards despite comments suggesting inlining.

Exits return stACME, not WACME or native ACME. External staking, bridge custody, validator operations and stACME redemption are not admitted or guaranteed. Direct stACMEMinter.deposit invokes bridge.burn to an unsupported-chain staking account and is excluded; owner mint/withdraw/admin methods are also excluded. Rewards require externally supplied surplus and underlying balance sufficiency; there is no implemented loss haircut/default-resolution path, so insolvency or accounting underflow may revert.

Wrapper full flattened source and ABI have Sourcify match creation/runtime grades, not exact_match. No bridge method is admitted.

Underlying stACME and wstACME share quantities use 8 decimals, inherited from underlying token decimals. deposit and mint pull only caller stACME and issue receiver shares. withdraw and redeem burn owner shares, requiring existing share allowance when caller differs from owner; no approval, permit or other authority is granted. Recipients need not be caller. Zero native value is required.

deposit rounds shares down and rejects zero shares; mint rounds required assets up; withdraw rounds required shares up; redeem rounds assets down and rejects zero assets. Empty supply uses one-to-one raw-unit conversion. No slippage/minimum-output parameter or wrapper fee exists in these bodies.

The xERC4626 ledger increases stored assets after deposits and decreases them before exits. totalAssets includes linearly unlocked prior-cycle rewards, not the entire observed token balance. syncRewards is permissionless fixed accounting only: it requires the prior cycle ended and positive surplus, incorporates the previous reward amount, and schedules surplus over a rounded next cycle (extended near the end). It does not pull funds or choose a recipient. Deposits do not themselves invoke syncRewards despite comments suggesting inlining.

Exits return stACME, not WACME or native ACME. External staking, bridge custody, validator operations and stACME redemption are not admitted or guaranteed. Direct stACMEMinter.deposit invokes bridge.burn to an unsupported-chain staking account and is excluded; owner mint/withdraw/admin methods are also excluded. Rewards require externally supplied surplus and underlying balance sufficiency; there is no implemented loss haircut/default-resolution path, so insolvency or accounting underflow may revert.
